name: e2e_bead_capture_assay_c2: lyse, incubate, mix
description: UNROUTED. Built by assay2chip/stages/s6_build.py from partition.json: op 7 lyse -> polygon_chamber 'lyse_7', op 9 incubate -> serpentine_channel 'incubate_9', op 10 mix -> herringbone_mixer 'mix_10'. lyse, mix, incubate share one board; they run between 20 and 20 C; 6 of the 6 ports allowed at demo scale; 29% of the envelope 30 x 20 mm (demo envelope), ONE fluidic layer at ONE 0.3 mm etch depth, base and lid 0.5 / 1 mm. COP (Zeonor 1060R) because hot_embossing route; 90 C max working temperature covers the 20 C hold; DNA adsorption Low: hydrophobic, little DNA binding; protein/enzyme adsorption possible. The hottest hold here is 20 C. SIZED FROM THE LOAD, never from the paper's tube volumes (assay2chip/README.md, 'Bench volumes do not transfer'): lyse_7 from 2,000 cells at 1500 per uL = 1.33 uL of suspension; incubate_9 from 2,000 cells at 1500 per uL = 1.33 uL of suspension; mix_10 from nothing is held: a stream with 120 s of residence. PLACEMENT: parts sit in flow order in 1 row(s) (left to right), spread across the usable 23.6 x 13.6 mm so the slack between them is routing corridor. Total chain length 41.8 mm, crossing risk 0, nothing rotated; every feature keeps at least 0.4 mm to its neighbours and to the chip edge. PORTS: 4 (inlet_1, outlet_1, reagent_in, waste), each over a PORT PAD the registry sized, so the bore opens entirely onto cut area and the port-overlap rule in tools/check_chip_spec.py passes. Inlets and outlets are on opposite edges, which is what keeps the layout planar in one layer, and no two ports are closer than 5 mm. CHANNELS BETWEEN PARTS ARE DELIBERATELY EMPTY: S7 routes them from assay2chip/work/<id>/connections_e2e_bead_capture_assay_c2.json. Until it has run, a chamber here is unconnected on purpose, and every rule that needs a channel - channel width against capsule diameter, channel crossings, protocol targets - can only be checked after S7. REALISED AS CHANNELS, not as parts: op(s) 8 (mix) - op(s) 8 (mix) carry a stream and nothing states a residence time, so there is no length or volume to build to; realised as the connecting channel rather than as a part. A conduit is sized from flow and residence time, and one that comes out smaller than a face a channel can attach to is not a small part but an unusable one, so it becomes the channel instead, lengthened to the length it needs. Parts sized by assay2chip/parts/registry.py. RISKS carried from sizing: SEDIMENTATION: a 50 um cell falls the full 300 um in 2.94 s but the residence time in the mixer is 42 s, so the cargo reaches the floor inside this part. Either keep the line moving, shorten the hold, or make the hold a chamber where settling is intended.; the 5 fold turns are not grooved, so about 12% of the path does not mix; the grooves are 60 um of relief in z and process z tolerance is +/-20 um (33% of the groove), so groove depth is the dominant fabrication risk in this part; the published staggered herringbone mixer uses ~50 um grooves; our in-plane floor forces 200 um grooves in a 1.2 mm channel, so this is a 4x scale-up of a published geometry and its mixing has NOT been measured here; this is a delay line, not a mixer: at Re << 1 folding adds residence time and nothing else (blocks.json herringbone_mixer is the mixing block).
